mainTopic: Reading grave markers, and when and how the court removes כלאים
overview: The גמרא finishes discussing a field where a grave was lost. It explains why trees in the field show that the grave area was plowed. רבי יהודה adds that we rely on this only when a זקן or תלמיד can confirm it. From this, אביי learns that a תלמיד חכם is responsible for his town's affairs. Next, רב יהודה and רבי אסי teach how to read marked stones and marked field borders. The basis for this is that a ציון is always placed right next to the טומאה. The גמרא then turns to our משנה's rule that inspectors go out for כלאים on חול המועד. It reconciles this with the משנה in שקלים about going out in אדר, and explains that workers are cheaper on חול המועד. That shows the workers are paid from the תרומת הלשכה. Finally, the גמרא starts to ask how much mixture counts as כלאים, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the grave is inside and the trees are outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that trees prove the grave spot was plowed. Maybe the trees stand only on the outer part of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the טומאה is on the inside and the trees are on the outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the sign of the trees. Maybe only the outer area near the trees was plowed, and the inner area with the grave was never touched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumed that trees in the field show the whole field was plowed. The challenge is that plowing near the trees proves nothing about the spot of the grave if the grave is deeper inside.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe (opens a doubt or challenge)
Ritual impurity; here, the grave that causes it
On the inside
On the outside
Trees

phrases.english: But perhaps the ritual impurity was on the inside
and the trees were on the outside?
phrases.notes: So maybe only the area by the trees was plowed, and the inner part with the grave was not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא (from before this section) that treats trees as proof the field was plowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that trees show the grave area itself was plowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The trees may only show that the outer area was plowed, not the inner area where the grave lies.

steps.title: The trees are spread throughout the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where the trees are scattered all over the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the trees are scattered throughout.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The trees are spread all over the field, so the whole field was plowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If trees are only on the edge, the doubt is real. But if they are mixed in everywhere, plowing around them covers the whole field, including the grave spot.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they are tangled or scattered throughout

phrases.english: Where the trees are scattered throughout.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Trees might only be on the edge, so the grave area might not have been plowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of trees spread across the whole field, so the whole field was plowed.

steps.title: A grave marker is placed close to the grave
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: a ציון is never placed far from the grave, so the trees near the marker are near the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: we already said that one does not place a marker far from the place of טומאה, so as not to cause a loss to ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the challenge. Since a marker is always set right next to the grave, the trees near the marker are also near the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Markers are kept close to the real grave so that good land is not needlessly treated as impure. So the plowed area around the trees must include the grave itself, even without saying the trees are spread out.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
We already said this
A marker warning of a grave
Place at a distance
To cause a loss

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general rule: grave markers are placed tightly so that as little of ארץ ישראל as possible is treated as impure.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: we already said:
one does not distance the marker from the place of impurity
so as not to cause a loss to the Land of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Using an earlier rule to remove the doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grave might be far inside, away from the trees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The marker sits right next to the grave, so the trees near it are near the grave, and the grave spot was plowed.

steps.title: Someone knowledgeable must confirm the facts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says we rely on these signs only if a זקן or a תלמיד is there to vouch for them, since not everyone knows the facts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: only if there is an elder or a student there, because not everyone is expert in the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא. רבי יהודה adds a condition: we need a knowledgeable person to confirm the signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary people may not know whether the field was really plowed. So רבי יהודה requires a זקן or תלמיד who knows what happened before we rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder, a respected scholar
A Torah student or scholar
Experts, well-versed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא שָׁם זָקֵן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד,
phrases.english: only when there is an elder or a student there,
because not everyone is well-versed in the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי יהודה's added condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The signs of plowing are relied on only when a זקן or תלמיד can confirm them.

steps.title: A Torah scholar is responsible for his town
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from רבי יהודה that a תלמיד חכם in a town carries responsibility for all the town's affairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: learn from this that a young Torah scholar who is in a town, all the town's matters are placed on him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a lesson from רבי יהודה's words. Since we count on the scholar to know about the field, he must be expected to know what goes on in his town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה assumed the scholar would know whether the field was plowed. אביי concludes that a תלמיד חכם is expected to be involved in, and know about, all the town's needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
A young Torah scholar
Town, city
Is placed, is thrown upon

steps.whatToRemember: Trees spread through a field, or near a marker, show the grave area was plowed; רבי יהודה requires a scholar to confirm; and אביי learns that a תלמיד חכם is responsible for his town's affairs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a well-known principle about the communal duty of a תלמיד חכם.

phrases.english: Abaye said: learn from this
a Torah scholar who is in a city —
all the affairs of the city are thrust upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from רבי יהודה's condition in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם in a town is responsible for all the town's affairs.

steps.title: How to read marked stones
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches: one marked stone means the ground under it is impure. With two stones, lime between them means the area between is impure; no lime means the area between is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: if one found a marked stone, the area under it is impure. Two stones: if there is lime between them, the area between them is impure; if there is no lime between them, the area between them is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about grave markers. רב יהודה explains what a stone marked with lime tells us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One marked stone marks the grave right under it. With two stones, lime on the ground between them shows they mark the two edges of one impure area. Without lime between them, each stone marks its own spot, and the space between is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A marked stone (signaling a grave)
Lime, a white substance used to mark graves
Underneath it
Impure / pure

steps.confusionAlert: Two marked stones do not automatically make the whole space between them impure. It depends on whether there is lime on the ground between them.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If one found a marked stone — underneath it is impure.
If two, if there is lime between them —
the area between them is impure,
and if there is no lime between them —
the area between them is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מָצָא אֶבֶן מְצוּיֶּנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about reading grave markers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One marked stone: impure underneath. Two stones: lime between them makes the area between impure; no lime means the area between is pure.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to depend on plowing, not lime
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a ברייתא: with two marked stones, the area between is טהור only if there was plowing between them, not because there is no lime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the area between the stones really pure even when there was no plowing? But a ברייתא teaches: one marked stone means the ground under it is impure. With two stones, if there was plowing between them the area between is pure, and if not, the area between is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's rule from the previous step. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to make plowing, not lime, the deciding factor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said that two stones with no lime between them means the area between is טהור. The ברייתא says that if there was no plowing between the stones, the area between is טמא, and it never mentions lime. So it looks like 'no lime' is not enough to make the area pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A marked stone, a sign that there is a grave
Plowing; signs that a plow went through
Between them, meaning the ground between the two stones

phrases.english: And even though there is no plowing?
phrases.notes: This is aimed at רב יהודה's rule from just before: two stones and no lime means the area between is pure.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: מָצָא אֶבֶן אַחַת מְצוּיֶּנֶת — תַּחְתֶּיהָ טָמֵא.
phrases.english: If one found one marked stone, underneath it is impure.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתַּיִם, אִם יֵשׁ חוֹרֶשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶן — בֵּינֵיהֶן טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: Two: if there is plowing between them, between them is pure,
and if not, between them is impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא חוֹרֶשׁ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's two-stone rule from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that two stones without lime between them leave the area between טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the area between טמא whenever there was no plowing, without any mention of lime, so 'no lime' alone does not seem to make it pure.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about lime poured on top of the stones
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is a case where lime was poured on the stones and spread around. Plowing could explain how lime got between them. Without plowing, the lime was meant to mark the ground between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here the case is where the lime was poured on top of the stones and spread thin this way and that. If there was plowing between them, the area between is pure, because we say the lime peeled off and fell there because of the plowing. If not, it is lime meant for the space between, and that area is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He says the ברייתא is a special case where there is lime between the stones, and plowing tells us how to read that lime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא there is lime on the ground between the stones too. If there was plowing, we can say the lime only fell there from the stones' tops, so the area between is טהור. If there was no plowing, the lime between them must have been put there on purpose to mark that ground, so it is טמא. This fits רב יהודה: lime between the stones means impure, and no lime means pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Lime (whitewash) used to mark a grave
Spread thin, flattened out
Peeled off, came off
In between, the space between the stones

steps.whatToRemember: Lime between two stones normally marks the space between as טמא. Plowing gives us another way to explain how the lime got there.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here it is where the lime is poured on their tops
and spread thin to here and to there.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִיכָּא חוֹרֶשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶן — בֵּינֵיהֶן טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: If there is plowing between them, between them is pure,
because we say it was due to the plowing that it peeled off,
phrases.notes: He means the plow knocked the lime off the stones onto the ground between them.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, סִיד דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי הוּא וְטָמֵא.
phrases.english: and if not, it is lime of the in-between, and it is impure.
phrases.notes: Without plowing, the lime between the stones was put there on purpose to mark that ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָכָא כְּשֶׁהַסִּיד שָׁפוּךְ עַל רָאשֵׁיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that plowing, not lime, decides whether the area between the stones is pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about lime spread between the stones. Plowing only explains that lime away. Without lime, רב יהודה's rule stands.

steps.title: How to read a field with marked borders
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי teaches that if one, two, or three borders of a field are marked, those borders are טמא and the field is טהור. If all four are marked, the borders are טהור and the whole field is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: If one border is marked, it is impure and the whole field is pure. If two are marked, they are impure and the whole field is pure. If three are marked, they are impure and the whole field is pure. If four are marked, they are pure and the whole field is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives a new teaching about marked borders around a field. Up to three marked borders, only the borders are טמא. With all four marked, the whole field inside is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When only some borders are marked, we read each mark as showing a grave in that border strip itself. When all four borders are marked, they surround the field, so the markers are pointing to the field inside as the impure place, and the borders themselves are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A border strip at the edge of a field
Marked as a place of impurity
The entire field

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that more marks always mean more impurity in the same place. With four marked borders, the borders become טהור and only the field inside is טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
One border is marked: it is impure,
and the entire field is pure.
Two: they are impure,
and the entire field is pure.
Three: they are impure,
and the entire field is pure.
Four: they are pure,
and the entire field is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי מֶצֶר אֶחָד מְצוּיָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on reading markers, moving from stones to marked field borders
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One to three marked borders: the borders are טמא and the field is טהור. Four marked borders: the borders are טהור and the field is טמא.

steps.title: Why four marked borders mean the field is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי אסי's four-border rule with a known teaching: a ציון is not placed far from the impurity, so that land in ארץ ישראל is not lost for no reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: We do not put a marker far from the place of impurity, so as not to cause a loss to the land of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי אסי's four-border rule. It quotes a teaching that a marker is always placed right next to the impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ציון is placed right next to the impurity, never far away. That way people do not avoid more land than they need to. So when all four borders are marked, the markers sit right at the edge of the impure area, and that area is the field they surround.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not place far away
A marker showing a place of impurity
To cause a loss

steps.whatToRemember: A ציון always sits right next to the impurity. That is why markers on all four borders mean the field inside is טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching keeps the marking system honest in both directions. Markers warn people away from real impurity, but they are not spread so wide that good land in ארץ ישראל goes unused.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
We do not distance a marker from the place of impurity,
so as not to cause a loss to the land of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: אֵין מַרְחִיקִין צִיּוּן מִמְּקוֹם טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the four-border case in רבי אסי's rule
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's ruling that four marked borders make the whole field טמא and the borders טהור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching ('דאמר מר') that a ציון is placed right next to the impurity so as not to cause a loss to ארץ ישראל

steps.title: The משנה's rule: inspectors go out for כלאים on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in our משנה that says officials go out even to deal with כלאים during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they even go out on חול המועד to deal with כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting another line from our משנה. It is setting up a question on this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists public needs that may be taken care of on חול המועד. One of them is sending people out to the fields to uproot כלאים, which are forbidden mixed plantings. The next step will question why this would be done on חול המועד at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures of plants that are grown together
The intermediate days of a יום טוב
They go out, meaning the court's inspectors go out to the fields

phrases.english: And they even go out to deal with diverse kinds.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about what's allowed on חול המועד. It means going out to pull up forbidden mixed plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of grave markers and quotes a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inspectors go out on חול המועד to uproot כלאים.

steps.title: Contradiction: the court already goes out for כלאים in אדר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a משנה in שקלים. That משנה says the court announces about כלאים on the first of אדר and goes out to deal with them on the fifteenth of אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really go out for כלאים on חול המועד? Here is a contradiction: on the first of אדר the court announces about שקלים and about כלאים. On the fifteenth of אדר the מגילה is read in walled cities, and they go out to clear thorns from the roads, fix the streets, and measure the מקוואות. They take care of all public needs, mark graves, and go out to deal with כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how our משנה can say they go out for כלאים on חול המועד. Another משנה says this job is already done on the fifteenth of אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the inspectors already went out in אדר, a month before פסח, the job should be finished. So why would they go out again on חול המועד? The two משניות seem to set different times for the same task.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other; the גמרא is pointing out a contradiction between two sources
The yearly half-שקל donation to the בית המקדש
Walled cities, which read the מגילה on the fifteenth of אדר
Public needs
Ritual baths

phrases.english: And do we go out for diverse kinds on Chol HaMoed?
And they raised a contradiction:
On the first of Adar they announce
about the shekels and about diverse kinds.
phrases.notes: This is the start of the first משנה in מסכת שקלים.

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ קוֹרִין אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה בַּכְּרַכִּים,
phrases.english: On the fifteenth of it, the Megillah is read in the walled cities,
and they go out to clear thorns from the roads,
and to repair the streets, and to measure the ritual baths.
And they take care of all public needs,
and they mark the graves,
and they go out to deal with diverse kinds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכִּלְאַיִם בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד נָפְקִינַן? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that they go out for כלאים on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in שקלים says the job is already done on the fifteenth of אדר, so there seems to be no reason to do it again on חול המועד.

steps.title: Two answers: the משניות are talking about different crops
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא each solve the contradiction. One says אדר is for the early crop and חול המועד is for the late crop. The other says אדר is for grains and חול המועד is for vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא: one said, here it is the early crop and there it is the late crop. The other said, here it is grains and there it is vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the contradiction. Both say the two משניות are about different plants, which can be recognized at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each answer, the first 'here' means the אדר משנה and the second 'there' means our חול המועד משנה. The early crop, or grains planted in winter, have grown enough by אדר to check them. The late crop, or vegetables, only show up later, so they are checked on חול המועד of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Early crop
Late crop
Grains and seed crops
Vegetables
One said; used when we do not know which of the two אמוראים said which answer

steps.whatToRemember: Going out for כלאים in אדר and going out on חול המועד do not contradict each other. Each time is for a different kind of crop that can only be recognized at that stage of the season.
steps.confusionAlert: In both answers, the first 'כאן' points to the אדר משנה and the second points to our חול המועד משנה. Do not mix them up.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: כָּאן בְּבַכִּיר, כָּאן בְּאָפִיל.
phrases.english: One said: Here it is the early crop, there it is the late crop.
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is the אדר משנה. The second 'there' is our חול המועד משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כָּאן בִּזְרָעִים, כָּאן בִּירָקוֹת.
phrases.english: And one said: Here it is grains, there it is vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: כָּאן בְּבַכִּיר, כָּאן בְּאָפִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each משנה is about a different kind of crop.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to be about the same plants, so the job should only need to be done once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אדר inspection covers early crops or grains, and the חול המועד inspection covers late crops or vegetables.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the אדר rule to when the blossom is not yet recognizable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: the משנה in שקלים, which says the court goes out on the fifteenth of אדר, applies only when the blossom was not yet recognizable. If the blossom was already recognizable, they go out to deal with the כלאים right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The rule about going out on the fifteenth of אדר applies only when the blossom is not yet recognizable. But if the blossom is already recognizable, they go out to deal with the mixed plants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a limit to the משנה in שקלים about going out on the fifteenth of אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date in the משנה is not fixed in every case. Workers can only tell which shoots are כלאים once the plants have blossomed. So if that is already clear earlier, there is no reason to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case of… (a phrase that limits a rule)
The blossom or bud of a plant
Recognizable, able to be identified
They go out over them, meaning the court's workers go out to deal with them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין נִיצָּן נִיכָּר,
phrases.english: They taught this only where the blossom is not recognizable,
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה in שקלים from step 12, about going out on the fifteenth of אדר.

phrases.english: but if the blossom is recognizable, they go out over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין נִיצָּן נִיכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the שקלים משנה that was just discussed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifteenth of אדר is the date only when the blossom cannot yet be recognized. If it can, the workers go out right away.

steps.title: Why go out specifically during the intermediate days of the Festival?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is special about חול המועד that the court sends its workers out then.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about חול המועד that we go out then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: why did our משנה pick חול המועד as the time to go out about כלאים? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we avoid work on חול המועד. So it seems odd to send workers out specifically then. The question is asking for the reason behind the timing, not challenging the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this case and not another?
We go out

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד דְּנָפְקִינַן?
phrases.english: What is different about the intermediate days of the Festival that we go out?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד דְּנָפְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to our משנה's ruling about חול המועד and asks for its reason
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the court chooses חול המועד to send out workers for כלאים

steps.title: Workers are cheaper during the intermediate days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן: the reason is the workers' wages. On חול המועד the workers charge us less.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is because of the workers' pay, which is cheaper for us at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The court goes out on חול המועד because hired workers cost less then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Workers cannot do their usual jobs on חול המועד, so they are willing to work for lower pay. The reason for the timing is about saving money, not about the plants.

keyTerms.meaning: Wages for work
They become cheap, they lower their price
For us, with us

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer about saving money is the basis for רב זביד's inference in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Because of the workers' wages, which are cheaper for us.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Workers' wages are lower on חול המועד, so the court saves money

steps.title: Inference: the workers are paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד (or רב משרשיא) learns from this answer that the workers are paid from the תרומת הלשכה. If the field owners paid them, the court would not care about saving money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד (some say רב משרשיא) said: Learn from this that when we pay the workers, we pay them from the public Temple fund. Because if you think the field owners pay them, why should we care? Let the owners pay them however much the workers want!
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא draws a new conclusion from רבי יוחנן's answer: the workers' pay comes from public Temple money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court only cares about cheap wages if it is spending public money. If the owners of the כלאים fields were paying, the court would have no reason to pick a cheaper time. So the concern for saving shows the money is from the תרומת הלשכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (an inference)
The fund collected from the half-שקל, kept in the Temple chamber for public needs
From theirs, meaning from the field owners' own money

steps.whatToRemember: The court goes out on חול המועד because workers are cheap then. That concern about cost shows they are paid from the public Temple fund, not by the field owners.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Zevid said, and some say it was Rav Mesharshiyya:
Learn from this:
when we give them wages,
we give it to them from the collection of the chamber.
For if it would enter your mind
that we pay them from theirs,
phrases.notes: "Theirs" means the owners of the fields where the כלאים grew.

phrases.english: what difference would it make to us?
However much they want, let them pay them!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, כִּי יָהֲבִינַן לְהוּ שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new halachic conclusion from the reason given in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The workers who remove כלאים are paid from the תרומת הלשכה. This is why the court tries to keep the cost low.

steps.title: How much mixture counts as diverse kinds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much of another species must be mixed into a crop for it to count as כלאים that must be removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the amount. How much of another kind of seed has to be mixed in before the workers must pull it out? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about when and how the court goes out. Now the גמרא asks about the size of the problem. A tiny amount of stray seed might not count.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much? What is the amount?

phrases.english: And up to how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who pays the workers to what amount of mixture requires removal
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of another species in a crop that makes it count as כלאים

steps.title: רב שמואל בר יצחק points to a משנה in כלאים
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers that the amount follows the משנה in כלאים, which begins: "Any סאה that has in it…" The quote continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: It is like what we learned in the משנה: Any סאה that has in it…
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יצחק starts to answer by quoting a known משנה about mixed seeds. The quote is cut off here and continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not invent a new amount. He ties the court's work to an existing rule about how much foreign seed can be in a measure of seeds. The exact amount appears in the rest of the quote.

keyTerms.meaning: Like that which we learned (in a משנה)
A measure of volume, used here for seeds

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:
Like that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כלאים 2:1.

phrases.english: Any se'ah that contains

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: כׇּל סְאָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 18 by citing a משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The amount follows the משנה in כלאים about a סאה of seeds containing another kind. The quote continues past this section.
